# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 13.08 ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. High = (13.08 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 57. A cap of 40 applies because `robots.txt` blocks Bingbot from the whole site, which goes against your declared policy of allowing AI search crawlers. The score is therefore 40. Most of the site is in good shape. It renders on the server, has titles, descriptions and canonicals, and has a sitemap. One `robots.txt` block, a missing sitemap line and a few small gaps hold the score down. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Bingbot - **Why it matters:** Bing's crawler is told to stay out of the whole site. Several AI search tools build on Bing's index, and your `geo.config.json` says AI search crawlers should be allowed. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small (delete those two lines and the blank line after them) - **Score after this:** 83/100 on its own. This lifts the cap and fixes GEO-009 and GEO-014 together. ### 2. Point `robots.txt` at your sitemap - **Why it matters:** `public/sitemap.xml` exists, but crawlers that read `robots.txt` are never told where it is. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt` (no `Sitemap:` line anywhere) - **What the code says:** the file ends at `Disallow: /` under `GPTBot`, with no `Sitemap:` line. - **Size:** Small (add `Sitemap: https://atlasroadmaps.example/sitemap.xml`) - **Score after this:** 40 on its own, because the cap stays until item 1 is done. With items 1 and 2 together: 92/100. ### 3. Put the changelog text in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** The changelog entries load in the browser after the page opens. A crawler that doesn't run JavaScript sees an empty list. - **Where:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` - **What the code says:** `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog').then((r) => r.json()).then(setEntries); }, []);` - **Size:** Medium (use a Remix `loader` so the entries render on the server) - **Score after this:** 95/100 once items 1 and 2 are also done. On its own it stays at 40 because of the cap. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers get the access you declared | Problem | `public/robots.txt:5-6`, Bingbot blocked site-wide. Blocker, cap 40. | | GEO-014 | Listed routes are indexable | Problem | `public/robots.txt:6`, Bingbot blocked on all 4 sitemap routes. No noindex on them; `/dashboard` is noindexed on purpose and not in the sitemap. | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on own domain | Problem | `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`, no canonical. Home, features and changelog are fine (3 of 4). | | GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Problem | `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5`, fetched in `useEffect` (3 of 4 routes clear) | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Searched for `ld+json` and `@type`, found none | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | `public/robots.txt`, no `Sitemap:` line. `public/sitemap.xml` is valid. | | GEO-012 | Title, description, html lang | Clear | `app/root.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. All indexable routes have a title and description. | | GEO-016 | Key routes reachable by links | Problem | `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`, `/features` is reached only through a clickable `
` (2 of 3 clear) | | GEO-017 | No snippet restrictions against AI search | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet` found anywhere | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `app/root.tsx` and all 5 routes. There are no images, and the links have text. | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt present | Not scored | None present | | GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | None present | ## Other problems found - `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`: `
navigate('/features')}>See all features
` isn't a link, so it can't be tabbed to or followed by crawlers. Replace it with ``. This is the same fix as GEO-016. ## Worth considering - **Add real plan details to the pricing page:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `Plans that grow with your team. Talk to us for a quote.` The page promises plans but names none. List plan names, what each includes and prices if you can share them. - **Give pricing its own title and description:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1` exports no `meta`, so it falls back to `app/root.tsx:2`, `{ title: 'Atlas' }`. Something like "Pricing | Atlas" with a short description would say what the page is. - **Back up the integrations claim:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Nothing says which tools. A named list, perhaps one page per integration, would answer what visitors will ask. - **Say more on the features page:** `app/routes/features.tsx:1`: `Timelines, sharing and status updates.` Each feature could get a short explanation and its own heading. - **Add `` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has no dates. The changelog already has real release dates. - **Link between pages in the content:** the home page links nowhere, and pricing and features don't link to each other. Add a footer with all main pages, plus links from features to pricing. - **Label the organization in structured data:** nothing states the site's identity in machine-readable form. Add `Organization` or `WebSite` JSON-LD in `app/root.tsx` with the name "Atlas" and your URL. - **Add head basics:** `app/root.tsx:6` has `` with no `charset`, `viewport` or social tags (Open Graph). Add them to `meta`. - **Hand-kept sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml` is a static file, so a new page must be added by hand. Generating it from your routes would keep it in step. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Real status codes and headers:** `X-Robots-Tag` and redirects set outside the repository aren't visible. A live check would show them. - **`/api/changelog`:** no route for it exists in this repo, so its source and content are unknown. ## Assumptions - Your declared policy in `geo.config.json` is to allow AI search crawlers and block training crawlers. The `GPTBot` block matches that, so I didn't count it. - I read all 9 tracked files: the root layout and navigation, all 5 routes (home, features, pricing, changelog, dashboard), `robots.txt`, the sitemap and the config. No JSON-LD exists, and no `.env` files were read. - I assumed Remix v2 meta behaviour, where a route's `meta` replaces the root's rather than merging with it. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
